subject.title: fix(memory-wiki): reject oversized apply body files

question: Should memory-wiki intentionally stop accepting synthesis body files above 1 MiB, and if so should that limit become a shared mutation contract across the CLI and `wiki_apply` tool?
rationale: The implementation can bound reads mechanically, but choosing a new public maximum and whether all entry points share it changes compatibility and requires owner intent.

options.title: Adopt a shared limit
options.body: Choose and document one body-size limit, enforce it at the mutation boundary across all public entry points, and retain the bounded reader for early rejection.

options.title: Preserve large-file support
options.body: Remove the new fixed rejection and refactor the synthesis write path so body files can be processed without an unbounded pre-mutation buffer.

options.title: Accept a CLI-only cap
options.body: Explicitly approve and document that `--body-file` has a lower limit than other synthesis input surfaces.

recommendation.title: Adopt a shared limit
recommendation.body: Choose and document one body-size limit, enforce it at the mutation boundary across all public entry points, and retain the bounded reader for early rejection.

likelyOwner.reason: The apply command and surrounding memory-wiki mutation behavior primarily originate from and have been maintained by this contributor.
